concept: Listbox is a list that stays open: every choice is printed inside one recessed window the same way Input holds a typed value, and the chosen rows carry a printed tick and weight, so nobody opens anything to learn what the panel can do.
family_difference: Listbox keeps its options open in a recessed window in the page, takes more than one choice, and has no trigger, chevron or floating panel.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Listbox as a stack of bordered cards with the chosen card filled blue or orange
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tinted fill tells the state by colour alone and spends a hue that P1 keeps for one part per unit; the printed tick and weight work in black and white.

default_to_avoid.pattern: native select element with the size attribute, drawn by the operating system
default_to_avoid.why_not: The system draws its own highlight and type, which ignore the material and cannot follow dial's light or keep a tick on the chosen rows.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): every band printed on the case at once, the one in use marked in ink
Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): settings printed beside plain plastic parts, no coloured marking

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The list is one window of surface.sunken with elevation.well and a line.ring hairline, the same recess as Input and the closed Select, full width of its column.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label is printed above the window at its start edge and names the list through aria-labelledby.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: A chosen row is told by a printed tick and medium weight in primary ink; no row is ever filled orange or blue.
The window sits in the page with only its inner well shade and no float shadow, because a list that stays open has nothing to leave.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: One tab stop, then arrows, Home, End, Page keys, type-ahead, Space and Enter choose, and in multiple mode Shift with arrows and Control with A extend the choice.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: A row inks in when it is reached and the tick fades with the choice; nothing moves while the list sits still.

options.name: rows inside one recessed well, tick and weight on chosen rows, the reached row a plate with a hairline
legend printed on the body with no container, an ink index bar beside chosen rows
raised plastic panel with seams between rows and a tick at the end

variants.reason: A gives the list an edge in the form column like Input and Select, so it reads as a field that takes a choice and its tick and weight work in black and white (P2 depth, P1 colour); B has no edge, so a long multiple list loses its column and its reached row, and C is a floating panel that repeats the open Select, though nothing here leaves (P6).

root.why: The field stacks the label above the window in one column and keeps the full inline size of that column.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the printing beside every other part of the unit.

list.why: The list is a recess with the inverse light, the same window that Input uses for typed text, so the rows read as cut into the body.

option.why: Every option row is at least 44px tall so a finger can pick it, with its text inset from the rounded ends.

tick.why: A printed tick in ink marks each chosen row, so a choice never uses the orange or any tinted fill; an empty tick keeps the column so words do not shift.

leading.why: An optional mark such as an icon or an avatar stands between the tick and the words on the same inset line, so rows with and without one still align.

text.why: Option words use the body size of the one grotesk, with a line box tall enough for stacked Thai marks, and long words wrap instead of being cut.

empty.why: A list with no options prints one plain line in secondary ink inside the window, so an empty list says so and the window never collapses.

md.why: The default row is 44px tall, the smallest target that every part in dial keeps for a finger.

lg.why: A 52px row with larger text for the main choice of a phone sheet held in one hand.

focus-visible.why: The whole list shows the same dark ring as every part when it holds keyboard focus, and the reached row inside it carries its own plate.

aria-selected=true.why: A chosen row is primary ink in medium weight with its tick, never a coloured fill behind the words.

aria-disabled=true.why: A disabled list loses its recess shadow and fades to half; a row that cannot be chosen fades to half and the arrows skip it, so both stay readable but are plainly not part of the walk.

data-active=true.why: The row under the keyboard or the pointer becomes a plate with a hairline, so the reached row is shown by depth and an edge, not hue.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the window keeps a real border, the reached row uses the system highlight and a chosen row keeps its tick.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion the rows and the tick still change on motion.hover, which the tokens keep, and nothing travels (D-008).

data-on=true.why: The tick of a chosen row fades in over motion.hover, so the choice is told by a printed mark that appears and not by a coloured fill.

background-color.why: The reached row sinks into a plate and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.

border-color.why: The reached row sinks into a plate and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.

color.why: The reached row sinks into a plate and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.

opacity.why: The tick fades in and out with the choice on motion.hover, so a change of choice is seen arriving.
